M15-01 recovery removed this from the mechanical path (closure is now measured against closure_scope, so the official count no longer decides the gate verdict), but the OFFICIAL contract count is still the owner's to ratify: 29 (drop A/B/C), 32 (ratify the addendum) or 39 (extend the contract). No number may be chosen by the chats. MEASURED 2026-10-27: the gate no longer reads the count, so all three options leave the verdict unchanged (709/0 in scope 3/3 either way). What changes is the work behind them: ratifying 29 means deleting M15-01-A/B/C from closure_scope and from expected_ids together (V-19a rejects a scope that names an undeclared id — fixture C-scope-blocked-member and the V-19a negative fixtures pin this), i.e. dropping the three items that currently carry evidence; ratifying 32 is a no-op (already emitted); ratifying 39 requires seven new items with their own evidence and scope entries. open_owner_decisions.why_it_blocks: No longer blocks anything. The owner ruled that direct oversight of the project continues and that a per-registry human signature is not a condition for passing the Strict Verification Gate; V-10 was removed from the gate, from the schema and from this builder, and the retirement is pinned by controls in the negative fixtures and by property P3 of the acceptance suite. The registry remains NOT VERIFIED for unrelated, honest reasons: 29 legacy items are UNKNOWN (V-15) and nothing was promoted to satisfy a gate.

open_owner_decisions.item: strict-verification.yml runs on push to arena/** while V-06 push mode requires HEAD to be an ancestor of origin/main
open_owner_decisions.state: NOT DECIDED (measured; both remedies remain owner decisions)
open_owner_decisions.why_it_blocks: A branch push can never satisfy V-06. Changing the trigger drops CI coverage; changing V-06 alters a security contract. Both are owner decisions. MEASURED 2026-10-27 on this exact head: the push-triggered run fails with exactly ONE failure out of 709 (V-06), and the pull_request run of the same commit passes 709/0, so the two runs together say "all 708 checks hold; the containment claim is not yet true because the branch is unmerged". The remedies, both still owner calls: (a) narrow the workflow trigger to pull_request + push:main (coverage of the pushed branch is then provided by the PR run of the same SHA — measured, not assumed: both runs execute against the same checkout), or (b) scope V-06 push mode to refs/heads/main and report the branch-push case as N/A-with-reason. (b) is a change to a security contract and must not be made by a chat; (a) is a CI-config change that moves, not removes, the enforcement point. Neither was applied: the failing step is left visible rather than silenced.

open_owner_decisions.item: Landing strategy for the registry-only metadata commit
open_owner_decisions.why_it_blocks: No longer blocks. Under binding_mode=lineage the rule is ancestry + witness blobs, not the shape of the landing commit, and that was measured on real topologies rather than argued: L1 a --no-ff merge commit (2 parents) keeps the binding valid (exit 0); L2 a squash landing is REJECTED because the evidence source stops being an ancestor (exit 1, "not an ancestor of the checkout") — so after a squash the evidence must be re-run and the registry re-emitted, which is a scheduling rule, not a rebind rule; L3 a commit that carries the registry AND files the evidence does not depend on is accepted; L4 the same commit is rejected when the extra file is witnessed. Practical consequence: merge, rebase and fast-forward are all legal landings now, squash is legal only with a re-emit, and the registry may ride with unrelated documentation. What remains the owner's is ordinary branch policy (which button the reviewer presses), not a gate constraint.
